title: Feralas
body: Feralas is a vast, rain-soaked forest in southwestern Kalimdor, green and wild beside the dry lands that surround it. Long ago the night elves built here, and their ruins lie everywhere beneath the canopy, above all the broken city of Eldre'Thalas, now called Dire Maul. Today the Gordunni ogres are the strongest power in the forest, and the land withers wherever they settle. On Sardor Isle, off the western shore, General Shandris Feathermoon holds Feathermoon Stronghold for the Alliance, the tauren of Camp Mojache keep the Horde's watch in the east, and the small way-station of Thalanaar stands on the border with the Thousand Needles. Neither side has the forest to itself. Woodpaw gnolls, Grimtotem tauren, Northspring harpies and Hatecrest naga each claim a share, a silithid hive festers in the southeast, and in the far north the great tree called the Dream Bough rises from an island in Jademir Lake, guarded by the green dragons of the Emerald Dream.

title: Thalanaar
body: Thalanaar is a small night elf way-station on the eastern edge of Feralas, where the forest gives way to the dry canyons of the Thousand Needles. It offers little more than a hippogryph roost, a pair of merchants and a trainer of tribal leatherworking, yet it matters more than its size suggests. The druid Falfindel Waywarder keeps his post here, and couriers from Feathermoon Stronghold cross the whole breadth of Feralas to bring him supplies. Travelers remark on how abruptly the green forest ends at this border. One scholar who studies the barren lands beyond is sure that strange magic was at work when that happened.

title: Camp Mojache
body: Camp Mojache is the Horde's foothold in Feralas, a tauren camp of hide tents built astride a swift stream above Wildwind Lake. Braves guard its paths, and it has an inn, a wind rider roost and trainers of many crafts. It is a meeting place as much as a village. The elder Talo Thornhoof tells his stories here, the troll Witch Doctor Uzer'i studies the spirits of beasts, the warrior Rok Orhan leads the fight against the ogres, and Krueg Skullsplitter has come on an errand from Orgrimmar. Its neighbors give it little peace. Woodpaw gnolls press up from the south with growing fury, and the Gordunni hold the river valley to the north.

title: Lariss Pavilion
body: North of Camp Mojache stands Lariss Pavilion, a large open-air hall raised in the old night elf style. It has two curious tenants. Azj'Tordin, a Highborne who slipped out of Dire Maul and the grip of its mad prince, lingers here, savoring the freedom for which he gave up his immortality. Nearby, the orc Xerash Fireblade prepares herb mixtures, and he trades them to Witch Doctor Uzer'i of Camp Mojache for such grim payment as the shrunken head of a dwarf. A door at the foot of the pavilion is said to lead back into the old city.

title: Gordunni Outpost
body: Following the river north from Camp Mojache leads to the Gordunni Outpost, a camp of the ogres who dominate Feralas. Ogres, brutes and ogre magi crowd it, and the land around them bears the scars of their presence. They guard more than their tents. The Gordunni bury a mineral called Gordunni cobalt in the earth here, betrayed only by its blue glow, and a goblin prospector newly arrived at Camp Mojache wants it dug up, sure it will fetch a pretty price. Soiled scrolls lie about the camp as well, and one of them depicts a dark ceremony performed by the ogre mage-lords, a puzzle the Horde is eager to solve.

title: Woodpaw Hills
body: South of Camp Mojache, the wooded hills belong to the Woodpaw gnolls, who keep a den deep among them. Mystics, reavers, trappers and brutes fill their camps, and their leaders call themselves Alphas. Their raids on the tauren have grown more frequent and more savage, as if the gnolls were desperate, and the reason lies on their own southern border, where they are fighting a second war against insects from the Writhing Deep. Like all gnolls they keep what they scavenge, and the packs of a missing Feathermoon courier were once found tacked to a tree in one of their camps. A rare treant, Gnarl Leafbrother, is sometimes seen among the hills.

title: The Writhing Deep
body: Beyond the Woodpaw camps in southeastern Feralas, the earth is broken into the twisted mounds and tunnels of the Writhing Deep, a hive of the insects known here as the Zukk'ash. Workers, wasps, stingers and tunnelers swarm over its slopes, and even the ore in its veins comes smeared with ooze. Among them roams Stinglasher, far larger than its kin and wrapped in an aura the others lack. Not every victim dies at once: the Zukk'ash seal captives alive in hard, mucous pods. Scholars in both Darnassus and Orgrimmar know the creatures by an older and more frightening name, the silithid.

title: Grimtotem Compound
body: East of Dire Maul, the Grimtotem tribe has raised a compound of tents in the Feralas woods, guarded by raiders, shamans and naturalists. These tauren are hostile to every outsider, and their work here is dark. In a bamboo pen nearby they keep captured sprite darters, the faerie dragons of the forest, for purposes no one has learned. Two night elves, Kindal Moonweaver and the priestess Jer'kai, keep watch over the camp from a rise above it. The Horde has taken notice too: in Orgrimmar, Belgrom Rockmaul has put a bounty on the clan's horns.

title: Dire Maul
body: In the heart of Feralas rise the broken walls of Eldre'Thalas, a city of Queen Azshara's Highborne, its great halls now called Dire Maul. The Queen is long gone, and the Shen'dralar who linger within have been marred by the madness of their Prince Tortheldrin. Gordok ogres hold the grounds outside, their hyenas prowling among the fallen stones, and in an arena within the walls, the Maul, ogre champions brawl while spectators such as Griniblix cheer them on. Deeper in, the wings hold satyrs, a rogue blood elf mage and perhaps the last refuge of a lost elven master.

title: The High Wilderness
body: The High Wilderness spreads across the uplands of southern Feralas, a broad country of forest glades and broken ground. Groddoc apes, ironfur bears and longtooth howlers roam it, Frayfeather hippogryphs wheel over its clearings, and Feral Scar yetis prowl its slopes. This was once night elf land, and its abandoned, ruined buildings still stand. The Gordunni ogres have claimed them, and where they dwell the trees wither and the ground is desecrated. The Feathermoon scholar Troyas Moonbreeze often comes here alone to study the ruins, much to the worry of Angelas Moonbreeze.

title: Ruins of Isildien
body: Deep in the High Wilderness lie the Ruins of Isildien, the remains of a large night elf city destroyed long ages ago. A broad stair climbs to a round hall that may once have been a temple. The Gordunni have made the ruins their stronghold, and here gather their mightiest: battlemasters, warlords, warlocks and the mage-lords whose dark ceremonies trouble the tauren of Camp Mojache. Their magic seems to wreak havoc on the very ground they stand on. Frayfeather hippogryphs still nest at the edges of the ruins, and an old bear called Old Grizzlegut is known to wander nearby.

title: Feral Scar Vale
body: Feral Scar Vale is a valley of yetis in southern Feralas, just inland of the Forgotten Coast. Its yetis grow hides so thick that leatherworkers in both Feathermoon Stronghold and Camp Mojache prize them, claiming that properly treated they are as strong as iron. A rare brute called Bloodroar the Stalker hunts the vale. In a cave nearby lies a stranger find: OOX-22/FE, a gnomish homing robot that looks rather like a chicken. It crashed here, and its maker in Booty Bay calls for someone to carry a beacon to it and escort it safely to the road.

title: Frayfeather Highlands
body: In the far south of Feralas, the Frayfeather Highlands are home to great flocks of wild hippogryphs: stagwings, skystormers and the proud patriarchs that lead them. Hippogryphs have been loyal companions to the night elves for many years, and their eggs can be found in nests across these heights. That loyalty has drawn unwelcome attention, for Witch Doctor Uzer'i of Camp Mojache covets the steadfast spirits of these birds for his muisek magic. The greatest of the flock, a hippogryph known as Antilus the Soarer, is seldom seen.

title: The Twin Colossals
body: Two immense peaks of rock tower over northwestern Feralas, the highest points in the land, and the road to Desolace runs between them. Mountain giants stride across the rocky ground at their feet, and Groddoc thunderers, ironfur patriarchs and rabid longtooths make every path dangerous. A few odd souls camp here. Marli Wishrunner can send a traveler to the top of a colossal, though only one way, and Kalin Windflight waits at the summit selling wings for the trip down. The gentle giant Rockbiter keeps a camp south of the Ruins of Ravenwind, and Gregan Brewspewer, a student of herbs who is hard to track down, keeps a camp out in these wilds.

title: Ruins of Ravenwind
body: West of the Dream Bough lie the Ruins of Ravenwind, remains of an ancient night elf city now overrun by the Northspring harpies. Their queen, Edana Hatetalon, is said to have a heart of crystal, empty of all but hatred, and she comes when a harpy horn is sounded by the Hatetalon stones in the northern ruins. Older magic lingers among the stones. Four flames named Samha, Imbel, Byltan and Lahassa still burn there, and the Equinex Monolith guards a secret that only an energized stave can open. On the eastern edge of the ruins, a gnoll named Miblon Snarltooth stands guard over a patch of evoroot.

title: The Dream Bough
body: In the far north of Feralas, Jademir Lake spreads its quiet waters around an island where a towering tree, the Dream Bough, rises above the forest. It is one of the great trees through which the Emerald Dream touches the waking world, and the green dragonflight guards it jealously. The dragons Lethlas and Dreamroarer keep watch over the island, and Jademir dragonkin patrol the lake shores and the grounds of Oneiros. At times a far greater shadow emerges from the Dream here: Emeriss, one of the great green dragons, now sick with corruption. Few mortals linger.

title: The Forgotten Coast
body: The Forgotten Coast is the western shore of Feralas, looking out across the water to Sardor Isle. Elementals of brine and sea spray rise from the surf, coast crawl creatures scuttle on the sand, and towering giants of the shore and the deep wade through the shallows. A dock here serves the ferry to Feathermoon Stronghold, and beside it the goblin Zorbin Fandazzle is trying, with growing doubts, to run an engineering shop. Not every boat makes its crossing. The wreck of a Feathermoon row boat lies in the muddy water nearby, its side torn open as if something had tried to snap it in two.

title: Sardor Isle
body: Sardor Isle lies off the Forgotten Coast, a forested island that the night elves of Feathermoon Stronghold have made their own. Beyond the stronghold's walls the island is wild. Coast crawl snapclaws and deepseers swarm its beaches, longtooth runners hunt in its woods, and a rare beast called Diamond Head lurks along its shore. South of the stronghold, the Ruins of Solarsal have fallen to the Hatecrest naga, and the Sentinels fear that the naga mean in time to seize the whole island. The Isle of Dread lies across the water beyond.

title: Feathermoon Stronghold
body: Feathermoon Stronghold is the Alliance bastion of Feralas, a night elf fortress on Sardor Isle reached by ferry from the Forgotten Coast or on hippogryph wings. General Shandris Feathermoon led an expeditionary force here and commands it still, with Feathermoon Sentinels on watch. It is a place of scholars as much as soldiers. Troyas and Angelas Moonbreeze pore over their books on the ruins of Feralas, the priestess Vestia Moonspear studies strange relics, the druid Quintis Jonespyre keeps a tree house, and a history of the Sentinels and the Long Vigil is kept for visitors. Its defenders watch two foes: the naga to the south and the Horde.

title: Ruins of Solarsal
body: The Ruins of Solarsal, on Sardor Isle south of Feathermoon Stronghold, are far older than any of the night elves' present works. The Sentinels once explored them, found nothing of note and left them in peace. Now the Hatecrest naga have filled them in alarming numbers: warriors, screamers, sirens and wave riders. At the heart of the ruins stands a gazebo that does not belong. It is clearly newer than the stones around it, its sides are engraved with a repeating band of unknown glyphs, and its stone is warm to the touch.

title: Isle of Dread
body: South of Sardor Isle, across the water, lies the Isle of Dread. Hatecrest serpent guards, myrmidons and sorceresses hold a deep cave at its northern end, Shalzaru's Lair, where Lord Shalzaru, one of the crueler naga royals, unearthed a strange relic. A hidden passage beneath the waves is said to lead to an inner chamber where Lady Szallah dwells. The heart of the island, a valley walled in by cliffs, belongs to beasts deadlier still: the chimaerok, great two-headed hunters, led by the mighty Lord Lakmaeran.

title: Shandris Feathermoon
body: Shandris Feathermoon is General of the Sentinel Army and the commander of Feathermoon Stronghold. Orphaned when the Burning Legion destroyed her village during the War of the Ancients, she was taken in by Tyrande Whisperwind and grew up at her side, through the Sundering and the long ages of the Sentinels, until she rose to lead them. In Feralas she weighs every move against the safety of her island. She would gladly throw her full strength against the Hatecrest naga, but she will not leave the stronghold open to the Horde. She also keeps ties to a quiet circle of the wary known as the Protectorate.

title: Latronicus and Vestia Moonspear
body: Latronicus Moonspear is Shandris Feathermoon's second, charged with meeting the naga directly. He has no patience for idle talk and is proud of his people's restraint: the night elves are no warmongers, he says, but they will act to protect their own. When the blood elf mage Lethtendris fled into Dire Maul with a web of stolen magic, it was Latronicus who called for agents to stop her. His wife Vestia is a priestess of the stronghold and one of its most learned scholars, and Latro, as she calls him when she forgets herself, brings her the puzzles he cannot solve.

title: Quintis Jonespyre
body: Quintis Jonespyre is the druid of Feathermoon Stronghold, a servant of Malfurion and the Cenarion Circle who keeps a little tree house within its walls. Curses are his specialty, and he can read the history of an object by touch, a draining art he calls psychometry. Lately he has been asking quiet questions about why Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm gathers so much morrowgrain in the Circle's name. The grain makes him uneasy, and he is sure something is amiss. His luck at cards is another matter. The stronghold calls him the King of the Bad Beats, and he owes Ginro Hearthkindle for his losses.

title: Troyas and Angelas Moonbreeze
body: Troyas and Angelas Moonbreeze are scholars of Feathermoon Stronghold who comb the ruins that cover the forests of Feralas for what they can tell of the past. Troyas is the bolder of the two. He ventures alone into the ogre-held High Wilderness, and from the rubble of the south he once pulled a stave that he was sure was more than it seemed, though a colleague in Rut'theran grumbles that he always thinks he has found something important. Angelas worries over him, and quietly asks travelers to thin the Gordunni in his path, begging them not to tell him. She also sends the curious to the goblin Marvon Rivetseeker to learn of the Sunken Temple.
sources: quest 2982 description and reward text (investigating the ruins; Troyas alone in the High Wilderness; don't mention a word to Troyas)
quest 2939 description and reward text (stave; Daryn: Troyas always thinks he has found something important)

title: Falfindel Waywarder
body: Falfindel Waywarder is a night elf druid posted at Thalanaar, on the border of Feralas and the Thousand Needles, and his name carries far beyond it. Keeper Albagorm of Stonetalon sends to him when great forest spirits are needed, the dying druid Heralath named him as the one who must be warned of the crone of Razorfen Kraul, and the couriers of Feathermoon Stronghold cross the forest to bring him supplies. He studies the corruption of Agamaggan's resting place in the Barrens and fears that its answer lies in treachery. He has noticed, too, that the Woodpaw gnolls to the south have grown strangely agitated.

title: Rockbiter
body: Rockbiter is a mountain giant who camps at the foot of the Twin Colossals, and for all his size he is gentle and plain of speech. His charge is a little night elf girl named Shay Leafrunner, and watching over her is harder than it sounds. Shay loves to wander and drifts away whenever something lovely catches her eye. When she slipped off from him in the ruins to the north, Rockbiter was sick with worry and hardly knew what to do. Shay has one weakness that always brings her running back, the sound of a precious bell she keeps, and Rockbiter is delighted to learn of it.

title: Talo Thornhoof
body: Talo Thornhoof is a tauren elder of Camp Mojache who is always glad to share his stories. In his day he was a seasoned hunter who feared no creature, until Northspring harpies ambushed him in the forest and he barely dragged himself to safety. He was never the same, and the hate still boils in him. He longs for revenge on the harpies and for the crystal heart of their queen, Edana Hatetalon. He still thinks like a hunter: know your enemy, he teaches, and he sends the bold to test the fel-maddened beasts of Felwood. When the blood elf Lethtendris carried her web into Dire Maul, Talo called for help.

title: Krueg Skullsplitter
body: Krueg Skullsplitter is an orc who traveled down to Feralas with his companions on a mission for his masters in Orgrimmar. Between duties he has a gentler errand. His life-mate Korrin takes great pleasure in new clothing, and he means to make her a cloak adorned with the shimmering wings of the sprite darters west of Camp Mojache. He warns that the little dragons can be dangerous and that the night elves in the forests are worse. News of Grimtotem in the woods alarms him. He calls the clan evil, wants their horns by the pile, and at last sends them to Belgrom Rockmaul in the Valley of Honor, who had set a bounty on them.

title: Azj'Tordin
body: Azj'Tordin is a Highborne who fled the halls of Eldre'Thalas and now lingers at the Lariss Pavilion. The Queen has long since passed, he says, and the works of the Shen'dralar have been marred by the madness of Prince Tortheldrin. He has traded his immortality for freedom and regrets nothing. In the haste of his escape, though, he was robbed. The imp Pusillin made off with his book of incantations and with the key to the once great halls. The key he no longer cares for. The book he wants back badly, and he waits for someone bold enough to chase the imp through the Warpwood Quarter.

title: Zorbin Fandazzle
body: Zorbin Fandazzle is a goblin engineer who has set up shop beside the dock on the Forgotten Coast against his own better judgment, and now suspects it may be the worst place imaginable. The giants of Feralas are bad for business, so he has built an Ultra-Shrinker, a gnomish shrinking ray improved with superior goblin know-how, and wants someone to try it on them. Then there are the sea elementals of the coast, whose water cores make fine fuel for his device. He insists there was never any danger, pays in coin and loot, and swears that his comrades in the Steamwheedle Cartel will hear of anyone who helps him.

title: Lonebrow's Journal
body: Henrig Lonebrow came to Kalimdor for the Explorers' League, hunting the bones of a fallen god in the Barrens, until the boar men of the Razorfen dragged him into the thorns of Razorfen Kraul. There he shared a hut with Heralath, a dying druid who had come to learn why the resting place of the boar god Agamaggan, held to be pure, had been so corrupted. Before his strength failed, Heralath begged the dwarf to carry word to Falfindel Waywarder at Thalanaar: the crone Charlga Razorflank was rousing her minions, and she had to be stopped before her corruption spread. Lonebrow escaped but never reached Thalanaar, and his journal was found on his body. Falfindel grieved for both brave souls. With no time to send word to Darnassus, he asked for a party to enter the Kraul and bring back the crone's medallion. Her death let the druids' studies go on, but Falfindel feared that the answer to the corruption lay in treachery.

title: The Hatecrest Naga
body: When the Hatecrest naga crowded into the Ruins of Solarsal, Shandris Feathermoon feared an attack on her island and sent an investigator south. At the heart of the ruins stood a gazebo, newer than the stones around it, carved with repeating glyphs and warm to the touch. The general found the report disturbing: whatever the naga intended, their presence threatened the night elves' push into Feralas. Unwilling to strip the stronghold while the Horde was near, she gave the matter to her second, Latronicus Moonspear. His plan was twofold: weaken the naga in numbers and command, and learn what they were doing in the ruins. Hatecrest scales were gathered, and scouts named a royal, Lord Shalzaru, who had dug up a strange relic in his cave on the Isle of Dread. Shalzaru was slain and the relic carried to Vestia Moonspear. It was not of naga design, she judged, but something far more alien, and she set to studying it.
sources: quests 2866, 2867, 3130, 2869, 2870, 2871 descriptions and reward texts
notes: Fact-check: Vestia's judgement reworded to match 2871 (not naga, something more alien).

title: The Missing Courier
body: Raschal had carried Feathermoon's messages since Shandris Feathermoon brought her expedition to Feralas. A week after he set out for Thalanaar, meaning to row down the coast and cross southern Feralas to avoid the Horde camp, he was declared missing, but his friend Ginro Hearthkindle would not give up. Raschal's boat was found wrecked off the coast, and in the mud lay his knife. The druid Quintis Jonespyre read it by touch and saw the courier carry two packs inland, meet the Woodpaw gnolls and return to his boat in terror, too distracted to notice water elementals forming behind him. The packs hung from a tree in a gnoll camp, holding a parcel for Thalanaar and a hasty note: Raschal had gone south to investigate strange insects in the Writhing Deep. There he was found sealed alive in a Zukk'ash pod. Shandris sent his report on the hive to the priestess Gracina Spiritmight in Darnassus, who knew the insects for silithid.
sources: quest 4281 (parcel for Falfindel)
notes: Fact-check: verified. Gracina (darnassus.json 165710) is only mentioned; her trigger is 4508, not 4267.

title: Freedom for All Creatures
body: From a rise above the Grimtotem Compound, Kindal Moonweaver and the priestess Jer'kai watched the tauren pen up sprite darters, and neither could guess why. Too few to fight their way in alone, they found a helper. Kindal took a bamboo cage key into the camp, threw open the pen and stayed beside the faerie dragons until they were safely away. Then the two elves took the fight to the Grimtotem, picking off naturalists, raiders and shamans until the clan was hunting them in turn. Jer'kai wondered whether other tauren frowned on these, as many races have less kindly cousins. With little to give, she sent her signet ring to High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind as word that they were well. The Moonweavers also saved a nest of eggs whose mother had died. One went as a gift to their helper, beginning a journey to the scholar Quentin at the Shimmering Flats and on to the animal handler Agnar Beastamer at Aerie Peak, where it hatched.
sources: quests 2969, 2970, 2972 descriptions and reward texts
quests 3841, 3842, 3843, 4297, 4298 (sprite darter egg, Quentin, Agnar Beastamer at Aerie Peak)

title: The Stave of Equinex
body: Searching the rubble of Feralas, Troyas Moonbreeze found a stave that looked ordinary, yet he could not shake the feeling that it was more. His books told him nothing, so he sent for help to his colleague Daryn Lightwind, a lore keeper in Rut'theran Village. She was unimpressed, grumbling that anything of value in those ruins had long since been hoarded by ogres or harpies. Still, she owned a worn old history of Feralas, and she would lend it for a price: a picture of Gammerita, a giant snapjaw of the Hinterlands, taken with the Super Snapper FX that the inventor Curgle Cranklehop built in Tanaris. With the book in hand, Troyas dared to hope that his find was the Stave of Equinex, the key to the Equinex Monolith in the Ruins of Ravenwind. Charged with the essence of the four ancient flames, it opened the monolith and gave up a stone that Troyas, reading on, identified as the Morrow Stone, a thing of great but unknown significance.
sources: quests 2939, 2940, 2941, 2944, 2943, 2879, 2942 descriptions and reward texts
notes: Daryn is female in the quest text (talk to her). Teldrassil's Rut'theran entry mentions her book only. Fact-check: the book's own page text is unreliable, so it no longer 'confirms' anything (2879 only says the stave might be the Stave of Equinex); 'sparkling' dropped.

title: War on the Woodpaw
body: To Hadoken Swiftstrider of Camp Mojache, the Woodpaw gnolls were a threat to the camp's very existence. They had always been driven back, but lately they pushed north more often and more savagely, almost as if they were desperate. Hadoken answered with a bounty on their manes, then with a stroke meant to break them: five of their Alphas slain in swift succession. Still he wanted to know what drove them, and a battle map taken from their camps told the tale. Most of its arrows pointed south, away from Mojache, and beside them was drawn a great insect with tally marks beneath. The gnolls were fighting on two fronts. South of their hills lay the Zukk'ash hive of the Writhing Deep. Its swarms were thinned and the giant Stinglasher was cut open for study, and Hadoken sent his findings to Zilzibin Drumlore in Orgrimmar, who named the insects silithid, a far worse threat than anything the Alliance could muster.
sources: quests 2862, 2863, 2902, 2903, 7730, 7731, 7732 descriptions and reward texts
notes: Fact-check: verified.

title: The Ogres of Feralas
body: In Orgrimmar, Belgrom Rockmaul called the Gordunni the dominant military force in Feralas and their growing numbers a danger to the Horde, and he sent the willing to the warrior Rok Orhan at Camp Mojache. She wanted the ogres pushed back, believing the land would heal once they were gone. North along the river, the ogres, brutes and ogre magi of the Gordunni Outpost were cut down. Then the fight moved to the High Wilderness, where stronger shamans, warlocks and maulers held old night elf ruins amid withered trees. A soiled scroll from the outpost raised a darker question. It showed a ceremony performed by the Gordunni mage-lords, and Rok Orhan sought one of their orbs, sure that a mage's orb held power enough to reveal the magic the ogres wield. A warrior, she could not tell what it was capable of. The orb went to the mage Uthel'nay in Orgrimmar, who found it fascinating, very powerful and very dangerous.
sources: quests 2981, 2975, 2980, 2978, 2979, 3002 descriptions and reward texts
notes: 2981 starts with Belgrom in Orgrimmar; 2978 starts from the Gordunni Scroll item. Fact-check: 3002 wording: she cannot tell what the orb can do.

title: The Muisek
body: Witch Doctor Uzer'i of Camp Mojache believes that great power lies in the muisek, the spirits of creatures slain in battle. When a beast dies violently, he teaches, its muisek may escape to seek revenge, even in the form of a greater creature. Shrink and capture the fallen at once, and the spirit is kept for use. His work began with a trade: a shrunken dwarf's head for herbs from Xerash Fireblade at the Lariss Pavilion, needed to prepare his vessel. Ironfur bears and longtooth runners came first. Then he turned on the allies of the night elves: hippogryphs for their loyal and steadfast spirits, faerie dragons for the strength hidden in their fragile bodies, treants for their power as protectors, and the mountain giants who left their peaks to stand with the kaldorei against the Burning Legion. With treant wood, minerals, sinew and metal fragments, he sealed the captured spirits forever into weapons for the Horde.
sources: quests 3121-3129 descriptions and reward texts
npc_text 1757 (Uzer'i on muisek)
notes: Fact-check: verified. 3128 (Natural Materials) has no prerequisite, so it is a second entry point.

title: Errands in Eldre'Thalas
body: Both camps of Feralas send champions into Dire Maul. Lethtendris, a blood elf mage whose brutality is matched only by her craving for magic, fled into the Warpwood Quarter among the satyrs and wove a web to snare the magical energies of the place. Heralds in the capitals call for agents, sending the Alliance to Latronicus Moonspear and the Horde to Talo Thornhoof. Latronicus means to release the web's power safely over the wilds, while Talo would give it to more responsible students of magic. Neither rejoices at her death. A quieter search is shared by two scholars, Sage Korolusk of Camp Mojache and Scholar Runethorn of Feathermoon, who work together despite their banners. They hunt for Kariel Winthalus, an elven master who fled the ruin of his homeland in Quel'Thalas with ancient artifacts, and followed his trail across the sea to Feralas. They believe he sought sanctuary in Eldre'Thalas, alive or dead.
sources: quests 7494, 7492, 7488, 7489 descriptions and reward texts
